ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 (effective 1 April 2023); Companies Act 71 of 2008, sections 50, 56A–56B and Regulations 32–34A of the Companies Regulations 2011, as amended by Act 22 of 2022 and the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; Financial Intelligence Centre Directive 6 of 2023 (verification of beneficial ownership); FIC Guidance Note 7 on Beneficial Ownership; Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act 37 of 2002 (FAIS) licensing overlay administered by the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory, risk-based, ongoing screening of all UBOs, directors, key individuals, and authorised officials against (i) the UN Consolidated List; (ii) the US OFAC SDN List; (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list; (v) the South African domestic terrorist and terrorist-related list published under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA); and (vi) domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs, including family members and close associates per FATF Recommendation 12 and FIC Guidance Note 4B). Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is triggered for any PEP, shell-company chain, or high-risk source of funds; screening evidence must be retained for at least 5 years after termination of the business relationship in accordance with FICA sections 28B–29 and FIC directives.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC eServices Companies Portal (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) — https://eservices.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name may be expressed in any of South Africa's 11 official languages but must be rendered exclusively in Latin (Roman) alphabetic script without non-Latin characters or diacritical ligatures. CIPC accepts English and Afrikaans as primary registry languages; names sourced from foreign languages must be transliterated phonetically into Latin script and accompanied by a sworn translation. A name may not be offensive, defamatory, or contrary to public policy, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, defensive name, or trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: CIPC statutory name reservations are valid for 180 days from approval; no statutory extension is available, but the applicant may lodge a new Form CoR 9.2 after expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant must (1) within 10 business days of the rejection notice, file alternative names via CoR 9.2; (2) simultaneously lodge a formal review application to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 using Form CTR-001 with the prescribed fee (approx. ZAR 1,000), attaching the CIPC rejection notice and legal submissions distinguishing the proposed name; (3) if the objection concerns a sensitive token in the prohibited list, apply directly to the Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition for consent under section 12(4) of the Companies Act; and (4) upon a favourable Companies Tribunal ruling, proceed with incorporation under the adjudicated name, preserving all appeal timelines before the High Court should Tribunal relief be denied.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited. The registered office must be a physical street address in South Africa where service of process and statutory records can be received per section 23 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; CIPC will accept a managed premises/commercial-space arrangement only if it is a real, staffed location. For the FSCA Category I Financial Services Provider licence required for retail equities, CFDs and derivative brokerage, a purely virtual or mailbox-only office is NOT permissible: the applicant must demonstrate operational premises, local compliance infrastructure, a fit-and-proper key individual, and physical records-management capacity in South Africa under the FAIS Act 37 of 2002 and FSCA conduct standards.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85–95% probability of an unannounced FSCA on-site inspection, thematic review, or prudential audit within the first 18 months of FSCA licensing for a retail equity/CFD brokerage; CIPC and the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) may also conduct unannounced premises inspections where AML/CFT red flags or supervisory concerns arise.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended; Sections 13, 14, 15, 16, 19 and 66
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the registered Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a private company may issue one or more shares of no par value. No escrow account or capital deposit is required under the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscribers hereby adopt the Memorandum of Incorporation as tabled. 2. The persons named as directors in the MOI are appointed as the first directors. 3. The registered office and postal address shall be as tabled. 4. The incorporation documents be submitted to CIPC and all filing fees be paid. 5. Each subscriber subscribes for the number of shares recorded opposite his/her name in the share register. 6. The first directors are authorised to open corporate bank accounts and to take all steps necessary to obtain regulatory licenses and commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge a name reservation application through CIPC eServices using the prescribed CoR 9.1 form. Submit up to four proposed names in order of preference and pay the name search fee. The reserved name is valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Identity or passport copies of each founding director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a fresh CoR 9.1 with alternative names or apply to the Companies Tribunal for name appeal within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Documents and Register the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit electronically the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the initial MOI, directors' consents and any required ancillary declarations. Pay the statutory incorporation fee via the CIPC payment gateway. Upon registration, the CIPC will issue an entity registration certificate and enterprise number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is queried, correct the noted deficiencies and resubmit the amended filing within 10 business days; alternatively, file a rectification application with CIPC once the company is provisionally registered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Governance Resolutions and Open Bank Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt the First Board Resolution, issue share certificates to subscribers, appoint the auditor or independent reviewer as required, and pass resolution(s) authorising the opening of segregated client and corporate bank accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any resolution or register is deficient, convene an extraordinary board meeting to ratify corrected resolutions and update the statutory records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for FSCA Securities Brokerage Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the FSCA licence application package for a Financial Services Provider (FSP) under the Financial Sector Regulation Act 2017 and FAIS Act 2002. Submit through the FSCA online licensing portal together with fit-and-proper declarations, business plan, AML/CFT policy, and compliance arrangements. Await licensing review and pay the applicable application fee when invoiced.
required_dossiers: Fit and proper declarations for directors and key individuals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSCA raises queries, remedy deficiencies within the prescribed response period. If the application is refused, apply to the Financial Services Tribunal for reconsideration or re-file once defects are cured.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Services Provider (FSP) Licence – Category I: Securities and Investment Services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based financial brokerage is not a listed activity requiring Full EIA Report or Environmental Registration under the NEMA EIA Regulations of 2014.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for process wastewater or VOC emissions; general domestic and office waste disposal must comply with municipal by-laws and the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the local municipal fire services; electrical installation certificate of compliance (COC) under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993; structural load inspection certificate for the office premises; workplace compliance certificate confirming first aid, emergency evacuation and occupational health protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), eFiling portal at www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity, including a (Pty) Ltd, must obtain an Income Tax Reference Number from SARS via eFiling or a SARS branch. For a South African-resident company, registration is mandatory and completed using forms such as IT77 and supporting documents including certified Memorandum of Incorporation, proof of foreign incorporation, beneficial ownership schedule, and appointment of a public officer. Non-resident entities with a South African permanent establishment must register for income tax under the Tax Administration Act and for VAT under the VAT Act if taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1 million or if the entity supplies electronic services to South African residents. SARS will issue a VAT registration number and income tax reference number, which must be renewed and maintained; failure to register may incur administrative penalties and interest.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no formal 'check-the-box' classification regime. A company incorporated in South Africa is automatically resident and taxable at entity level. Foreign-incorporated entities may elect to be treated as South African residents if their place of effective management is in South Africa. Controlled foreign company elections are available under s.9D for exclusion of high-taxed income. For VAT, a foreign vendor may apply to register as a separate vendor or for group VAT treatment in certain circumstances, and may elect to account for VAT on the invoice or payments basis subject to SARS approval.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1 million (mandatory for taxable supplies made in South Africa; non-resident electronic services suppliers are required to register if supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 per 12-month period, subject to SARS binding general ruling)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. VAT invoices must be issued in electronic or paper form containing prescribed particulars under s.20 of the VAT Act. SARS requires electronic filing of VAT returns via eFiling or a SARS-approved API. SARS is implementing e-invoicing standards based on PEPPOL BIS 3.0 but, at present, there is no mandatory real-time pre-clearance or continuous transaction control requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of movable goods qualify for 0% VAT if the supplier exports the goods within 90 days of supply and retains proof of export. For services, zero-rating applies where services are supplied to a non-resident person not present in South Africa at the time the services are rendered, provided the services are not supplied under a taxable supply chain to a South African recipient. Offshore securities brokerage services supplied by a (Pty) Ltd to foreign clients may be zero-rated if the brokerage services are directly rendered outside South Africa and the beneficial recipient is a non-resident, supported by contracts, KYC, and payment documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) showing physical export from South Africa
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) from an authorised South African bank
Proof of non-resident status of the overseas client (e.g., passport copy, certificate of residence, KYC file)
Brokerage service agreement and settlement instructions evidencing offshore service delivery
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may audit zero-rated export supplies and deny zero-rating if documentary proof is inadequate. Failure to export within 90 days or to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days may result in retrospective output VAT at 15% plus interest. Under the Tax Administration Act, understatement penalties range from 10% to 100% depending on the degree of non-disclosure; deliberate tax evasion may carry criminal penalties including imprisonment. The general anti-avoidance rules may be applied to artificial arrangements designed to obtain undue VAT refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the delegated authority of the Minister of Finance, with the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961 promulgated under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act No. 9 of 1933). Authorised Dealers, being the major commercial banks, administer day-to-day exchange control decisions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand is fully convertible for current account flows (trade in goods and services, dividends, interest, and branch remittances) processed by Authorised Dealers without SARB reference, subject to documentary substantiation. Capital account items remain controlled on the outward leg: residents require Authorised Dealer or FinSurv approval for outbound investments, foreign loans, and guarantees, whereas non-resident inward equity investment is unrestricted. Profit remittance and dividend payments to non-resident shareholders are permitted once the inward investment has been registered as an Inward Listing/Investment Certificate with an Authorised Dealer, Dividends Tax (20%, subject to treaty relief) has been settled, and SARS tax compliance status is verified where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: South Africa has abolished the historical 100% surrender ratio and the requirement to immediately convert export earnings into rand; however, all export proceeds, including fees and commissions earned from non-resident brokerage clients, must be repatriated to the Republic within 180 days from date of invoice/trade completion and must flow through a local Authorised Dealer, either to a ZAR account or to the exporter's designated Foreign Currency Account maintained with that Authorised Dealer. 100% of proceeds must be accounted for on the export/service declaration and, where conversion is made, must be routed at the ruling market rate; no partial surrenders or retention of proceeds offshore are permitted absent prior FinSurv approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with segregated client trust (Section 4(b) FAIS) sub-account; Capital Escrow Account for inward FDI receipts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: FirstRand Bank Limited (First National Bank / RMB Private Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account plus GSPS-style segregated client money account; RMB dealing desk for FX forwards
Multi-currency Flexi Account; segregated broker trust account; corporate treasury account
Operational Account and segregated client trust account for FAIS-regulated brokers
Operational Account with trade finance overlay; Export/FCA account linked to foreign brokerage receivables

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium for operational treasury purposes but legally prohibited as a client-money custodian: offshore digital EMIs (for example Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer, Currencycloud) are neither licensed deposit-takers nor Authorised Dealers under the SARB Prudential Authority framework, and cannot hold FSCA-mandated segregated client money for a securities broker. Such EMIs may be engaged only as a supplementary disbursement corridor for non-client operational expenses, while all brokerage settlement and client capital flows must be transmitted via SWIFT MT103 through a South African Authorised Dealer; moreover, a resident company's maintenance of funds at a foreign EMI constitutes an offshore bank account that requires FinSurv approval under the Exchange Control Regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence is effectively required for a high-risk financial-services legal person: under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (Act 38 of 2001, as amended) and the FIC Guidance Notes, the Authorised Dealer must positively identify all beneficial owners (natural persons holding at least 5% ownership or effective control) and the accountable company officers. In practice Standard Bank, FirstRand, Investec, and Absa require the directors, the Compliance Officer, and the FICA Authorised Representative to appear face-to-face at a registered South African branch (Johannesburg or Cape Town) for an EDD interview before final mandate approval; remote opening is generally declined for this risk tier unless the principals hold a pre-existing private-banking relationship, in which case a notarised identity and source-of-wealth pack with commissioner-of-oaths attestation may be accepted as supplementary evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners (≥5% shareholding or effective control) without a documented source of wealth and source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified source-of-wealth file comprising audited remuneration/salary records, investment realisation contracts, inheritance or trust deeds, certified by a commissioner of oaths or apostille; bank reference letter issued by the remitting foreign bank within 6 months; notarised affidavits from each beneficial owner; independent verification obtained via a registered South African audit firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions negative-media hits against directors, shareholders, or the originating jurisdiction (OFAC/UN/EU listings or FATF grey-list status).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full sanctions and adverse-media screening report (World-Check or equivalent) for all directors and beneficial owners; jurisdiction risk assessment citing FATF and Basel AML Index; independent AML memorandum distinguishing hit-for-name from true positive; remediation governance plan and written undertaking to restrict flows from sanctioned counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Brokerage operating without an FSCA FAIS licence or pending licence application, creating suspicion of unlicensed financial services conduct.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FSCA licence or formal acknowledgement of licence application; appointment record of the Regulatory Compliance Officer; Fit-and-Proper registers for all representatives; compliance manual and statutory mandate templates; professional indemnity insurance certificate; SARB FinSurv confirmation letter if cross-border exemptions are claimed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume outward remittances to foreign executing brokers and custodians which could be characterised as disguised capital flight rather than trade settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade and clearing confirmation trail: client order tickets, executing broker statements, custodial statements, Commercial LC or MT103 vouchers; Form A exchange control applications filed with the Authorised Dealer; monthly transaction-monitoring report; SARS tax compliance status verification evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client or shareholder funding sourced through crypto-asset exchanges or virtual-asset service providers into the dealing account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-rail-only funding policy approved by the AML Committee; blockchain analytics report (chain-analysis) for any digital-asset linked funds; proof that counterparties are licenced/registered VASPs under FIC Schedule 1; enhanced CDD file on each such client; ongoing transaction monitoring alert review certificates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant non-resident equity injection: the foreign shareholder remits by SWIFT MT103 to the broker's operating account at a South African Authorised Dealer, with the payment narrative 'Share capital subscription — inward direct investment in unlisted private company (ZA_PTY_LTD)'. The Authorised Dealer captures the transaction as an Inward Listing (Form IL / Inward Investment Certificate), applies the prevailing ZAR market rate, and credits the capital to the company's ZAR account; the company must evidence the subscription through a board resolution, an updated Companies Act 71 of 2008 section 56 beneficial-ownership register, issued share certificates, and the investors' source-of-funds declarations before the funds are released for operational use. The Inward Listing number becomes the permanent exchange-control identity quoted on all subsequent dividend and capital repatriations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound brokerage settlements (fees to foreign executing brokers, clearing and custody charges, client pay-outs) move via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV from the entity's Authorised Dealer account, each disbursement supported by a Form A outward transfer application and an underlying voucher (invoice, contract, client order, or clearing statement). Where a Commercial Letter of Credit is used for trade-linked payments, the issuing Authorised Dealer opens an MT700 documentary credit in favour of the offshore beneficiary; local ZAR disbursements settle in real time through the SARB SAMOS RTGS platform, and every payment is reconciled against the deal-level liquidity pool to demonstrate non-speculative, arms-length trade purpose.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forwards (FX forwards) with a local Authorised Dealer, strictly hedging verified brokerage income or committed payables, with tenors not exceeding 12 months and zero speculative open positions.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) executed to hedge foreign-currency borrowings or long-term receivable exposures, provided the underlying loan/asset has been declared to FinSurv and the hedging nexus is confirmed by the Authorised Dealer.
Vanilla European-style currency options used to hedge firm committed transactions, with the option premium and strike reflecting arm's-length commercial parity.

Restricted instrument note: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing the South African rand are NOT permissible for onshore resident entities, as the Exchange Control Regulations prohibit any structure establishing an offshore rand conversion market; only deliverable instruments settled in ZAR through an Authorised Dealer satisfy exchange-control requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (registered office, directors and company particulars confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Pretoria, South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of ZAR 1,000 (approx. USD 55) per overdue annual return; failure to file for two or more consecutive years permits removal of the company from the register under s82(3) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, causing administrative strike-off and loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register and annual UBO confirmation return (filed with the annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Pretoria, South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, simultaneously with the CIPC annual return; any change to beneficial ownership must be filed within 7 business days of the triggering event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and shareholders may be liable on conviction to a fine of up to ZAR 1,000,000 and imprisonment of up to 24 months under s213(2) of the Companies Act, as amended by the General Laws (AML/CFT) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; CIPC rejects the annual return, triggering deregistration risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: FSCA audited annual financial statements and FAIS annual compliance report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA), Menlyn, Pretoria, South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, audited AFS within 6 months of financial year-end; FAIS compliance report and licence renewal submission between 90 and 30 days before the annual licence anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty of up to ZAR 1,000,000 per contravention under s30 of the FAIS Act 37 of 2002; suspension, restriction or withdrawal of the securities brokerage licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: FSCA / National Treasury annual financial sector levy and licence renewal fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA), Menlyn, Pretoria, South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, on or before the FSP licence renewal date (renewal cycle measured from the licence anniversary).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrear levies attract prescribed interest; persistent non-payment results in refusal or withdrawal of the FSCA licence and statutory debt collection by the National Treasury.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SARS corporate income tax return (ITR14) and provisional tax finalisation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), Pretoria, South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, ITR14 within 12 months of the financial year-end; provisional tax payments by the end of months 6 and 12 of the year of assessment, with a top-up payment within 6 months after year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Understatement penalty of up to 200% of the tax shortfall under s222 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011; 20% penalty for material underestimation of provisional tax; interest at the prescribed rate (approx. 10.5% p.a.); criminal fines of up to ZAR 50,000 for non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) Risk and Compliance Return (RCR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC), Centurion, Pretoria, South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, covering the preceding calendar year, submitted between 1 January and 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative sanctions under the FIC Act 38 of 2001 ranging from remedial directives to a maximum administrative penalty of ZAR 10,000,000, depending on the severity of the non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to the (Pty) Ltd securities broker as a licensing condition under s83(2) of the Financial Markets Act 19 of 2012 and the FAIS Act 37 of 2002, irrespective of turnover. Under general company law (Companies Act s30(7) read with Companies Regulations 2011, reg. 23), a non-public-interest private company must appoint a registered auditor if its Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or higher; an independent review is required for PIS between 100 and 349; below 100 neither audit nor review is required unless the MOI or a regulator imposes otherwise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS as issued by the IASB, applied in South African Rand (ZAR) pursuant to s29(1)(a) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; IFRS for SMEs is not acceptable to the FSCA for a licensed Category I / OTC-derivative securities intermediary. Annual financial statements must be prepared within 6 months of the financial year-end and approved by the board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On each incorporation anniversary the (Pty) Ltd must file the Beneficial Ownership Return with the CIPC together with the annual return, reconfirming all natural persons holding a direct or indirect interest of 5% or more. Share transfers must first be registered in the Register of Members, and the beneficial ownership register must be updated and lodged with CIPC within 7 business days of any transfer or change. The BO register must be retained at the registered office and produced to the CIPC, FIC or FSCA on demand, with CDD information verified in accordance with the FIC Act 38 of 2001.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400-2,500 per annum (registered office, corporate secretarial services, CIPC lodgement and FSCA compliance liaison)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000-20,000 per annum (IRBA-registered registered auditor for a dual-licensed broker holding segregated client assets)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; no tiered rate for financial institutions
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Africa grants no general tax holiday. Relevant reliefs for a (Pty) Ltd brokerage: exemption of dividends received (s10(1)(k)); foreign tax credits (s6quat); indefinite assessed-loss carryforward under s20 (no statutory expiry; subject to s20A anti-loss-trading rules); s11D R&D allowance (generally unavailable to a pure retail brokerage); small business corporation 21% rate is unavailable to an entity with investment income or performing financial intermediation.
